articles.title: ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंकमा नागरिक एपबाटै खाता खोल्न सकिने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंक लिमिटेडले नागरिक एपसँगको सहकार्यमा नागरिक एपमार्फतै बैंक खाता खोल्न सकिने नयाँ सुविधा सुरु गरेको छ ।

राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्रका आधारमा नागरिक एपमा आबद्ध नेपाली नागरिकले बैंकको वेबसाइटमा उपलब्ध क्यूआर कोड स्क्यान गरी व्यक्तिगत बचत खाता अनलाइनबाटै खोल्न सक्नेछन् ।

यो सेवा १८ वर्ष वा सोभन्दा माथिका राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्र भएका तथा नागरिक एपमा आबद्ध व्यक्तिका लागि उपलब्ध हुनेछ । खाता खोल्ने क्रममा बैंकले ग्राहकको पूर्वसहमतिमा आवश्यक व्यक्तिगत विवरण नागरिक एपबाट सुरक्षित रूपमा प्राप्त गर्ने भएकाले पुनः विवरण भर्नुपर्ने झन्झट हट्ने, गोपनीयता कायम रहने र सूचनाको सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित हुने बैंकले जनाएको छ ।

नागरिक एपमार्फत खोलिएको खाता सञ्चालनका लागि भने ग्राहकले नजिकको शाखामा गई वा भिडियो केवाईसीमार्फत प्रमाणीकरण गर्नुपर्नेछ ।

बैंकका अनुसार सरकारी डिजिटल पूर्वाधारको उपयोग गर्दै सुरु गरिएको यो सेवाले खाता खोल्ने प्रक्रियालाई थप सहज, सुरक्षित, पारदर्शी र प्रविधिमैत्री बनाउनेछ । ग्राहकलाई आधुनिक डिजिटल बैंकिङ अनुभव प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास बैंकको छ ।

ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंक ७७ वटै जिल्लामा शाखा सञ्जाल विस्तार गर्ने निजी क्षेत्रको पहिलो वाणिज्य बैंक हो ।

हाल बैंकले ३४२ शाखा, ३६८ एटिएम, १४७ शाखारहित बैंकिङ सेवा, ६९ एक्सटेन्सन तथा राजस्व सङ्कलन काउन्टर र ३ वटा वैदेशिक प्रतिनिधि कार्यालयसहित १ हजारभन्दा बढी सेवा केन्द्रमार्फत सेवा दिँदै आएको छ ।

articles.title: मेलम्चीमा स्थानीय उत्पादन प्रवर्द्धनका लागि ‘कोशेली घर’ उद्घाटन
articles.summary:
मेलम्ची । स्थानीय कृषि र हस्तकला उत्पादनलाई प्रवर्द्धन गर्ने उद्देश्यले सिन्धुपाल्चोकको मेलम्ची बजारमा नयाँ व्यावसायिक केन्द्र “कोशेली घर” सञ्चालनमा आएको छ। साउन ८ देखि हरेक दिन बिहान ७ बजेदेखि राति ७ बजेसम्म खुल्ने यो कोशेलीघरको उद्घाटन नगरप्रमुख आइतमान तामाङले गरेका छन् ।

नगरप्रमुख तामाङले कोशेलीघरबाट ताजा फलफूल तथा तरकारी, घरेलु अचार, मह, भान्साका आवश्यक परिकार, हस्तकला सामग्री, अण्डा, माछा, गेडागुडी, चिया, कफी तथा हर्बल सामग्रीलगायत स्थानीय रैथाने उत्पादनको सीधा बिक्री वितरणमा जोड दिने बताए । उनले यहाँ राखिने विशेष परिकार तथा उत्पादनहरू आवश्यक परेमा जिल्ला बाहिर पनि पठाइने समेत जनाए ।

कोशेलीघरले स्थानीय उत्पादक र उपभोक्तालाई एउटै छानामुनि प्रत्यक्ष भेटघाटको व्यवस्था गराउँदै बजारसम्म पहुँच सहज बनाउने लक्ष्य लिएको प्रमुख तामाङले बताए ।

साथै प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत निमेष मिश्रले ‘फार्म देखि किचनसम्म अवधारणाअनुरूप उत्पादक र उपभोक्ताको मागअनुसार नयाँ वस्तु तथा उत्पादनहरू परिष्कृत गरी सार्वजनिक गरिने र उद्यमीहरूको भेटघाट हुने उपयुक्त स्थलको रूपमा यसलाई विकास गर्ने योजना रहेको बताए । प्रारम्भिक अनुमान अनुसार नगरपालिकाले दैनिक हजारौंले यहाँबाट किनमेल गर्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

मेलम्ची आसपासका सरकारी तथा निजी कार्यालयका कर्मचारी, घुम्न आउने पर्यटक, स्थानीय टोल तथा छिमेकी पालिकाका बासिन्दाहरू प्रमुख लक्षित ग्राहक रहने कोशेलीघरबाट स्थानिय रोजगारी र व्यवसायिक गतिविधिलाई थप सक्रिय बनाउन मद्दत पुग्ने उपस्थित उपभोक्ताले विश्वास व्यक्त गरिएको थियो ।

articles.title: २४ औं अनसन शुरु, समर्थनसँगै विरोध पनि बढ्दै
articles.summary:
कैलाली । धनगढीस्थित कृष्ण मन्दिर धर्मशालामा डा. गोविन्द केसीको सत्याग्रह दोस्रो दिन पनि जारी छ । स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्र सुधारका पाँचबुँदे माग अघि सार्दै उनले शहीद दशरथचन्द स्वास्थ्य विज्ञान विश्वविद्यालय र चिकित्सा शिक्षा आयोगमा स्वार्थ बाझिने नियुक्ति खारेज गर्न, चिकित्सा शिक्षा ऐन संशोधन गर्न, छात्रवृत्ति कटौतीको निर्णय फिर्ता लिन र मापदण्ड नपुगेका निजी मेडिकल कलेजमा थप सिट स्वीकृति रोक्न सरकारसँग माग गरेका छन् ।

विगतका सहमति कार्यान्वयन, चिकित्सा शिक्षालाई गैरनाफामूलक बनाउने तथा भ्रष्टाचार र अपराधका आरोपमाथि निष्पक्ष अनुसन्धानको मागसमेत डा. केसीले गरेका छन् । डा. केसीले आफू विश्वविद्यालयको विरोधमा नभई स्वार्थ बाँझिने नियुक्तिको विरोधमा सत्याग्रहमा बसेको स्पष्ट पारेका छन् ।

यता शहीद दशरथचन्द स्वास्थ्य विज्ञान विश्वविद्यालय संघर्ष समितिले भने डा. केसीलाई सत्याग्रह स्थगित गर्न आग्रह गरेको छ ।

संयोजक लोकराज पाण्डेको नेतृत्वमा प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारीलाई भेटेको टोलीले आन्दोलनका कारण विश्वविद्यालय सञ्चालन र विकासको प्रक्रिया प्रभावित हुन सक्ने भन्दै आवश्यक पहल गर्न अनुरोध गरेको हो ।

उता, कृष्ण मन्दिर धर्मशाला व्यवस्थापन समितिले पूर्वसूचना बिना अनिश्चितकालीन सत्याग्रह सुरु गरिएको भन्दै डा. केसीलाई स्थान खाली गर्न पत्र दिएको छ । तर डा. केसीले व्यवस्थापन समितिसँग सहमतिमै सत्याग्रह सुरु गरेको दाबी गर्दै केही स्वार्थ समूहले आन्दोलन कमजोर पार्ने प्रयास गरिरहेको आरोप लगाए ।

उनले दबाब र अवरोधका बाबजुद आफ्ना मागबाट पछि नहट्ने र आवश्यक परे फुटपाथमै बसेर पनि सत्याग्रहलाई निरन्तरता दिने बताएका छन् ।

चिकित्सा शिक्षा सुधारको मागसँगै डा. केसीको आन्दोलन जारी रहँदा विश्वविद्यालय सञ्चालनमा असर पर्ने चिन्ता भने स्थानीय स्तरमा बढ्दै गएको छ ।

articles.title: २ लाख ऋण, १४ लाख तिर्दापनि जग्गा बैंकको कब्जामा !
articles.summary:
सप्तरी । सप्तरीको विष्णुपुर–६ मा माय जलपा बचत तथा ऋण सहकारीका अध्यक्षले ऋणीहरूको धितो जग्गा फिर्ता नगरी आफ्नै परिवारको नाममा नामसारी गरेर बैंकमा धितो राखेको आरोप लागेको छ । बैंकले लिलामी सूचना प्रकाशित गरेपछि पीडितहरू ठगीको तथ्य थाहा पाएसँगै जग्गा फिर्ता र दोषीमाथि कारबाहीको माग गर्दै न्यायको खोजीमा भौतारीरहेका छन् ।

सप्तरीको विष्णुपुर गाउँपालिका–६ रञ्जितपुरकी रेणु देवी दासले २०७२ सालमा माय जलपा बचत तथा ऋण सहकारी संस्था लिमिटेडबाट छोरीको विवाहका लागि दुई लाख रुपैयाँ ऋण लिएकी थिइन् । उनले ब्याजसहित पटक–पटक गरेर करिब १४ लाख रुपैयाँ तिरेर तीन वर्षअघि नै ऋण चुक्ता गरिन् । तर सहकारीका अध्यक्ष दिलिप यादवले घरको लालपुर्जा फिर्ता दिन आलटाल गर्दै आएका छन् ।

अहिले मल्टीपर्पस् फाइनान्स बैंकले उक्त घरजग्गा लिलामीको सूचना प्रकाशित गरेपछि सहकारी अध्यक्षको कर्तुत सार्वजनिक भएको छ भने पीडित परिवार न्यायको खोजीमा भौतारिएको छ । अनुसन्धानका क्रममा सहकारीका अध्यक्ष यादवले जग्गा आफ्नो पत्नी सुनिता यादवको नाममा नामसारी गराई सोही जग्गा धितो राखेर बैंकबाट ऋण लिएको आरोप लागेको छ । बैंकले लिलामी सूचना जारी गरेपछि मात्रै पीडितले आफ्नो जग्गा अर्कैको नाममा रहेको थाहा पाएका हुन् ।

लिलामी सूचना देखेपछि रेणु दास बैंक पुगेर आफ्नो जग्गाबारे जानकारी मागेकी थिइन् । बैंकले ऋण बराबरको रकम तिरेपछि मात्रै जग्गा फिर्ता गर्न सकिने जनाएको उनको भनाइ छ । त्यसपछि उनले सहकारी अध्यक्षलाई बैंक जान आग्रह गरे पनि उनले अस्वीकार गर्दै सम्पर्कबाट टाढिएका छन् ।

यस्तै स्थानीय पुलकित मुखियाले पनि ५० हजार रुपैयाँ ऋण लिएर धितो राखेको एक कठ्ठा जग्गा ऋण चुक्ता गर्दा समेत फिर्ता नपाएको र आफ्नो नामबाटै नामसारी गरिएको आरोप लगाएका छन् ।

पीडितहरू सहकारीका सञ्चालकले सम्पत्ति बेचेर फरार हुने आशंकामा छन् । उनीहरू आफ्नो जग्गा फिर्ता गराइ दोषीमाथि कारबाही गर्न सम्बन्धित निकायसँग न्यायको माग गरिरहेका छन् ।

articles.title: उजाड पाखामा चिया खेती, गाउँमै रोजगारी
articles.summary:
दोलखा । दोलखाको कालिञ्चोक गाउँपालिका–४ सुन्द्रावतीमा व्यावसायिक चिया खेतीले गाउँमै रोजगारी सिर्जना गरेको छ । बाँझो जमिन हरियो चिया बगानमा रूपान्तरण भएपछि महिला, ज्येष्ठ नागरिक र युवाले दैनिक १८ सय रुपैयाँसम्म आम्दानी गर्दै स्थानीय आर्थिक गतिविधिमा उल्लेख्य टेवा पु¥याएका छन् ।

दोलखाको कालिञ्चोक गाउँपालिका–९ सुन्द्रावतीमा व्यावसायिक चिया खेतीले गाउँको स्वरूप फेरिएको छ । रोजगारीको अभावका कारण हुने युवा पलायन र बाँदर आतंकजस्ता समस्याको समाधान गर्दै चिया खेती स्थानीयका लागि आयआर्जनको भरपर्दो माध्यम बनेको छ ।

पहिले उत्तिसको घारीले ढाकिएको र झुसुले किराको समस्याले विद्यालयका विद्यार्थीसमेत प्रभावित थिए । तर यो क्षेत्र वडा कार्यालयको पहलमा सफा गरी इलामबाट ल्याइएका २५ हजार चियाका बिरुवासहित हरियो चिया बगानमा रूपान्तरण गरिएको छ ।

प्रारम्भिक परीक्षण सफल भएपछि यसको व्यवस्थापनको जिम्मा स्थानीयको सहभागितामा बनेको सुन्द्रावती चिया विकास समूहलाई हस्तान्तरण गरिएको छ । ७–८ वर्षको अन्तरालमा यहाँ उत्पादित चियाले बजार पाउन थालेको छ ।

प्रति किलो १०० रुपैयाँका दरले चियाको मुना टिप्ने व्यवस्था भएपछि महिला, ज्येष्ठ नागरिक र परीक्षा दिएर बसेका विद्यार्थीले गाउँमै रोजगारी पाएका छन् । बिहानदेखि साँझसम्म काम गर्ने मजदुरले दैनिक १८ सय रुपैयाँसम्म आम्दानी गरिरहेका छन् ।

वडा कार्यालयको बजेट र लगानीमा अघि बढाइएको यस योजनामा चालु आर्थिक वर्ष मात्रै ४ लाख रुपैयाँ थप लगानी गरिएको छ । चिया प्रशोधन सहज बनाउन ६ लाख रुपैयाँ लागतमा तीन प्रकारका आधुनिक प्रशोधन मेसिनसमेत सञ्चालनमा ल्याइएको छ ।

स्थानीय सरकारको सही योजना र निरन्तर लगानी भए बाँझो जमिनलाई पनि आम्दानीको स्रोत बनाउन सकिने उदाहरण सुन्द्रावतीको चिया खेतीले प्रस्तुत गरेको छ ।

articles.title: मारुती सिमेन्टद्वारा जयन्ती मेमोरियल ट्रस्टलाई CPR तालिमका लागि म्यानिकिन हस्तान्तरण
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । हालको परिवेशमा विशेषगरी युवापुस्तामा अस्वस्थ जीवनशैली, अत्यधिक तनाव तथा हृदयसम्बन्धी आकस्मिक समस्याका घटनामा वृद्धि हुँदै गएको अवस्थालाई मध्यनजर गर्दै CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation) तालिमको आवश्यकता बढ्दै गएको छ।

यही आवश्यकतालाई महसुस गर्दै मारुती सिमेन्ट लिमिटेड ले आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्व (CSR) अन्तर्गत देशभर CPR तालिम सञ्चालन गर्ने उद्देश्यका साथ जयन्ती मेमोरियल ट्रस्ट लाई आवश्यक CPR Training Manikin हस्तान्तरण गरेको छ।

उक्त सामग्री हस्तान्तरण कार्यक्रम दुवै संस्थाका सञ्चालक तथा पदाधिकारीहरूको उपस्थितिमा सम्पन्न भएको हो। कार्यक्रममा मारुती सिमेन्ट लिमिटेडले समाजप्रतिको आफ्नो उत्तरदायित्व निर्वाह गर्ने प्रतिबद्धतालाई व्यवहारमा उतार्दै स्वास्थ्य सचेतना अभिवृद्धिमा सहयोग पुर्‍याउन पाउँदा खुशी लागेको जनाएको छ।

जयन्ती मेमोरियल ट्रस्टले प्राप्त CPR Training Manikin को प्रयोग गरी देशभर निःशुल्क वा पहुँचयोग्य CPR तालिम सञ्चालन गर्ने, आकस्मिक हृदयाघात वा अन्य आपत्कालीन अवस्थामा सर्वसाधारणले समयमै प्राथमिक उपचार प्रदान गर्न सक्ने जनशक्ति तयार गर्ने लक्ष्य रहेको जनाएको छ।

ट्रस्टका अनुसार CPR सम्बन्धी ज्ञान र सीपको विस्तारले आकस्मिक अवस्थामा बहुमूल्य जीवन बचाउन महत्वपूर्ण योगदान पुग्ने विश्वास गरिएको छ। यस सहकार्यले समुदायमा स्वास्थ्य सचेतना बढाउनुका साथै जीवनरक्षा सम्बन्धी सीप विकासमा महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका खेल्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: सैनिक कल्याणकारी भवन ठेक्का प्रकरण : निर्माण व्यवसायीमाथि चरम अन्याय र अर्बौँको लगानी जोखिममा !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । काठमाडौँको न्यूरोड महाँकालस्थानस्थित सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषको स्वामित्वमा रहेको व्यावसायिक भवन भाडामा लिई अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ लगानी गरेको श्रीजयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रा. लि. चरम प्रशासनिक थिचोमिचो र अन्यायमा परेको निश्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।

भवन हस्तान्तरणमा सेनाकै तर्फबाट भएको ढिलाइ, काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकासँगको नक्सा पास विवाद र कोभिड–१९ को महामारीका कारण उत्पन्न विषम परिस्थितिलाई नजरअन्दाज गर्दै कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयले उल्टै निर्माण व्यवसायीमाथि एकतर्फी रूपमा करोडौँ बक्यौताको भार थोपरेको पाइएको हो । यस विषयमा अहिले सर्वोच्च अदालतमा मुद्धा पुगेको छ । साथै यस विषयमा मानव अधिकार आयोगमा पनि उजुरी परेको छ ।

प्राप्त दस्तावेज तथा पत्राचारका अनुसार सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोष र श्रीजयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रा. लि. बीच २०७६ माघ १६ गते महाँकालस्थानस्थित ‘कल्याणकारी भवन’१५ वर्षका लागि भाडामा लिने सम्झौता भएको थियो । सम्झौताको मुख्य सर्त नै भवन विधिवत रूपमा पूर्ण निर्माण भई हस्तान्तरण भएपछि मात्र भाडा लागू हुने भन्ने थियो । तर, बोलपत्र जारी गर्दाकै बखत उक्त भवनको नक्सा पास नभएको र मापदण्ड विपरीत बढी निर्माण गरिएको भन्दै काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाले काम रोकेपछि सम्झौताको प्रारम्भिक चरणमै विवाद उत्पन्न भएको थियो । सैनिक कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयको आफ्नै आन्तरिक र कानुनी त्रुटिका कारण समयमा भवन हस्तान्तरण हुन नसकेको बताइन्छ ।

पुरक सम्झौताको उल्लंघन र कोभिडको मार

भवन हस्तान्तरण हुन नसकेपछि दुवै पक्षबीच वि.सं. २०७८ मङ्सिर २८ गते पुरक सम्झौता गरियो, जसमा भवन हस्तान्तरणको मिति २०७८ असार १ कायम गर्ने प्रयास गरियो । तर, सो अवधिमा देशव्यापी रूपमा फैलिएको कोभिड–१९ को दोस्रो लहर र लकडाउनका कारण भवन पूर्ण रूपमा तयार भई व्यापारिक प्रयोजनका लागि हस्तान्तरण हुनै सकेन ।

व्यापार व्यवसाय ठप्प भएको र बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्थाबाट कर्जा प्रवाह नभएको यस्तो गम्भीर आर्थिक मन्दीको समयमा नेपाल सरकार रक्षा मन्त्रालयले समेत भाडामा छुट दिन निर्देशन जारी गरेको थियो । सैनिक कोषको आफ्नै कार्यदलले भाडामा ५० प्रतिशत छुट दिने राय पेस गरेपनि निर्देशनालयका केही अधिकारीहरूको बदनियतका कारण व्यवसायीले पाउनुपर्ने उक्त कानुनी छुट रकम उपलब्ध गराइएन ।

प्रशासनको उल्झन

निर्माण कम्पनीका एकल शेयरधनी खगेन्द्र बुढामगरका अनुसार, खण्डहर अवस्थामा रहेको भवनलाई अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ निजी लगानी गरेर मासिक ५ करोड ६३ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी भाडा उठ्ने सुनिश्चित व्यावसायिक केन्द्र बनाएपछि सैनिक कोषका केही अधिकारीहरूको ‘गिद्धे नजर’ यसमा परेको हो ।

कम्पनीले पटक–पटक पारदर्शी हिसाब मिलानका लागि लिखित अनुरोध गर्दा समेत त्यसलाई बेवास्ता गर्दै उल्टै पानी र बिजुलीको लाइन काट्ने, लिफ्ट प्रयोग गर्न नदिने र कम्पनीका कर्मचारीहरूमाथि कार्यस्थलमै भौतिक आक्रमण गर्नेसम्मका निकृष्ट कार्यहरू भएका छन् । जसले गर्दा व्यवसायी मानसिक र आर्थिक रूपमा पूर्णतः धराशयी हुने अवस्थामा पुगेका छन् ।

निष्पक्ष छानबिन र हिसाब फरफारकको माग

नेपाली सेनासँग लामो समयदेखि विकट भूगोल र ब्यारेकहरूमा समेत निर्माण कार्य गरी व्यावसायिक सम्बन्ध कायम राखेको यस कम्पनीले रक्षा मन्त्रालय, प्रधानसेनापति कार्यालय र बालाध्यक्ष विभागमा बोधार्थ दिँदै एक उच्चस्तरीय निष्पक्ष छानबिन टोली गठन गर्न माग गरेको छ । कम्पनीले सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषलाई कुनै रकम तिर्नु बुझाउनु पर्ने बाँकी नरहेको, उल्टै कल्याणकारी कोषको तर्फबाट भएको सम्झौता उल्लंघन र अनाधिकृत रकम असुलीका कारण आफूले अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ क्षतिपूर्ति पाउनुपर्ने दाबी गरेको छ । राज्यको शक्तिशाली अंगको आडमा एउटा वैधानिक निर्माण व्यवसायीको निजी सम्पत्ति र लगानीमाथि गरिएको यो चरम दोहनले नेपालमा निजी क्षेत्रको लगानी कति असुरक्षित छ भन्ने गम्भीर प्रश्न खडा गरेको छ ।

भवन ठेक्कामा करिब २० करोड हिनामिना आरोप

काठमाडौँको न्यूरोड महाँकालस्थानस्थित सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषको स्वामित्वमा रहेको व्यावसायिक भवन ठेक्का प्रकरणमा तत्कालीन सैनिक कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयका उच्च अधिकारी र कर्मचारीहरूको मिलेमतोमा झण्डै २० करोड रुपैयाँ बराबरको ठूलो आर्थिक हिनामिना भएको गम्भीर आरोप लागेको छ । श्रीजयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रा। लि। का एकल शेयरधनी खगेन्द्र बुढामगरले सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषका तत्कालीन उच्च अधिकारी र हालका प्रमुख अवकाशप्राप्त जर्नेल सुनिल राज विष्ट,कर्मचारीहरू नानिराम थापा र कर्णबहादुर तामाङ लगायतले शक्तिको दुरुपयोग गरी अर्बौँको निजी लगानी डुबाउन खोजेको आरोप लगाएका छन् ।

श्री जयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रालिबाट भवन व्यवस्थापन कार्यालयमा पदस्थापन भएका नानिराम थापा,कर्णबहादुर तामाङ लगायत त्यहाँ कार्यरत कर्मचारीहरुको मिलेमतोमा उक्त भवनमा श्री जयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रालिले उठाउनुपर्ने भाडा बिजुली महसुल र क्याम्प चार्ज असुल गरेको आरोप लागेको हो ।

त्यस्तै,यो टोलीले निर्माण व्यवसायी खगेन्द्र बुढामगरसँग मात्र होइन,त्यस भवनमा व्यवसाय गरिरहेका विभिन्न व्यापारीलाई नाम सारी तथा राम्रो लोकेशनको पसल उपलब्ध गराइदिने प्रलोभनमा पारी रकम उठाइरहेको बुढाको गम्भीर आरोप छ ।

त्यसैगरी बुढाका अनुसार यी पात्रहरुले अदालतलाई समेत विभिन्न माध्यमबाट दबाब सिर्जना गर्ने र मुद्दालाई कम्जोर बनाएर आफ्नो काला कर्तुतहरु लुकाउन खोजेको उनले बताएका छन् ।

कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयले बोलपत्र आह्वान गर्दा भवनको नक्सा पास नै नभएको र महानगरको अवरोधका कारण निर्माण कम्पनीले समयमा काम सुरु गर्न नपाएको, भवन पूर्ण रूपमा निर्माण नै नभई र खण्डहर अवस्थामा रहँदा समेत निर्देशनालयले पुरै अवधिको पूर्ण भाडा दाबी गरी पत्र पठाउनु कानुनी रूपमा त्रुटिपूर्ण रहेको, कम्पनीले आफ्नै खर्चमा जडान गरेको ट्रान्सफर्मर, विद्युतीकरण, खानेपानी प्रणाली, र लिफ्ट जस्ता पूर्वाधारहरू कल्याणकारी भवन व्यवस्थापनले एकतर्फी रूपमा नियन्त्रणमा लिई व्यवसायीलाई प्रवेशमा रोक लगाएको आरोप लागेको छ ।

भवन व्यवस्थापनकै केही कर्मचारीहरूले व्यापारीहरूबाट सोझै करिब १ करोड ३५ लाख विद्युत महसुल र क्याम्प चार्ज उठाएको साथै २०७९ साल श्रावण,भदौ र असोज ५ गतेसम्मको पुरै भवन भाडा श्री जयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रालिको बैंक ग्यारेन्टीबाट असुल गरेको र त्यहाँ व्यवसायी गरिरहेका ब्यापारीहरुबाट समेत असुल गरी सो रकम हिसाबमा मिलान नगरी गायब पारेको अर्को गम्भिर आरोप पनि छ ।

कम्पनीको नाममा रहेको मिटर तथा बिलिङ सफ्टवेयर नक्कली हस्ताक्षर प्रयोग गरी अनाधिकृत रूपमा नामसारी गरिएको र कम्पनीले अर्बौँ खर्चेर बनाएका संरचनाहरू सहमति बिना भत्काएर दोहन गरिएको आरोप छ ।

त्यस्तै,अहिले यस विषयमा मानव अधिकार लगायतका स्वतन्त्र निकायहरुले वास्तविक छानबिन गरिरहेको र सर्वोच्च अदालतमा समेत मुद्दा चलिरहेको निर्माण व्यवसायी बुढा मगरले जानकारी दिए । उनका अनुसार सर्वोच्च अदालतले १५ श्रावणमा दुबैपक्षलाई छलफलका लागि बोलाएको हुँदा उक्त छलफलबाट सकारात्मक नतिजा आउने बुढा मगरले विश्वास गरेका छन् ।

articles.title: एनसेल अब सरकारको नाममा आउने, सर्वोच्चको बोल्ड फैसलापछि वालेन्द्रको परीक्षा शुरु
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । एनसेल निजी क्षेत्रको अग्रणी सञ्चार माध्यमको रुपमा स्थापित कम्पनी हो। तर, एनसेलले नेपालमा गरिरहेको व्यापार र सेवा प्रवाह भने विवादास्पद नै छ। कर प्रकरणदेखि अन्य विषयमा समेत लम्बेतान विवादमा फसेको एनसेलको सेयर किनबेचपछि भने यसबारेका प्रश्नको सवालमा सर्वोच्च अदालतको आदेशपछि थप कानूनी प्रष्टतासहित अवैध गतिविधिविरुद्ध नेपालले आफ्नो कानूनको कार्यान्वयन गर्न सक्षम छ भन्ने सन्देश दिएको छ ।

लामो समय कर विवादमा फसेको एनसेल नेपालको अग्रणी निजी क्षेत्रको टेलिकम सेवा प्रदायक बन्न पुग्यो। नेपालको टेलिकम क्षेत्रमा नविनताका निम्ति काम गरेको एनसेलले सञ्चारको क्षेत्रमा खेलेको भूमिकामाथि प्रश्न गर्ने ठाउँ छैन्।

अझं भन्नुपर्दा सरकारी स्वामित्वको नेपाल टेलिकमले दिने सेवालाई एनसेलले दिएको चुनौतीकै कारण सञ्चार क्षेत्रले नेपालमा राम्रो स्तरको सेवा प्रवाहमा काम गरेको पाइन्छ। तर, एनसेलको यो राम्रो पाटोसंगै विवाद भने अत्यन्तै महत्वपूर्ण छन्। हरेक वर्ष मनग्य आम्दानी पनि दिएको एनसेलले विदेशमा नोपलबाट ठूलो धनराशी पठाएको छ।

सेवासंगै मेवा पनि दिएको एनसेलले केहि विवाद यस्ता पनि भोग्यो, जुन नेपालको कानूनको प्रत्यक्ष उल्लङ्घन र राज्यविरुद्ध गरेको एकखाले अपराध नै हो। कर छली विवाद लामो समयसम्म लम्बिदा एनसेलले आफ्ना भौतिक संरचनामा क्षति व्यहोर्ने स्थिति बन्यो। अझं, तत्कालीन विप्लव नेतृत्वको नेकपाले एनसेलको कार्यालयमा बम विस्फोट गराएपछि सेक्युरिटी गार्डले ज्यान नै दिने स्थिति बन्यो। यसरी देशभरका विभिन्न क्षेत्रका भौतिक संरचनामा किन आक्रमण भए? यसका पछाडी कारण हुन्, एनसेलले नेपालको कानून पालना गर्न भन्दा बढि मुनाफा आर्जन गर्ने ध्येय राख्नु।

सेयर खरिदबिक्रीको घोटाला

एनसेलले गरेको सेयर खरिदबिक्री भने अस्वभाविकमात्रै थिएन, सार्वभौम मुलुकको स्वाधिनतामाथिको प्रहार नै थियो। नेपालले निर्माण गरेको कानून व्यवसायमैत्री थिएन भनेपनि त्यो कानून नेपालको सार्वभौमसत्तासंग जोडिएको विषय थियो।

नेपालको संसदले निर्माण गरेको कानून नेपालभित्र सबैलाई मान्य र बाध्यकारी हुन्छ। तर, एनसेलको हकमा यो लागू नहुने गरि गरिएको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीमा सर्वोच्चको झड्कापछि भने नेपालले आफ्नो कानूनको पालना निर्वाध गराउनसक्छ भन्ने प्रष्ट सन्देश दिएको छ ।

सेयर खरिदबिक्री अमान्य

सर्वोच्च अदालतका न्यायाधीशद्वय सपना प्रधान मल्ल र टेकप्रसाद ढुंगानाको संयुक्त इजलासले विवादास्पद सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई अमान्य र अस्वभाविक भन्दै खारेज गरिदिएको छ।

यसले एनसेलको अध्यक्ष बन्न पुगेका सतिसलाल आचार्य अब कर्मचारीको हैसियतमा पुगेका छन भने एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व रेनोल्ड होल्डिङ्स लिमिटेडको वास्तविक मालिक मलेसियन कम्पनी आजियाटाकै रहेको ठहर गरेको छ। सतिसलालको कम्पनी स्पेक्ट्रलाइट युकेले किनेको भनिएको ८० प्रतिशत सेयर अमान्य भएको छ ।

के भन्यो सर्वोच्चले ?

सर्वोच्च अदालतले एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व ६ अर्ब हाराहारीमा भएको कारोबारलाई अमान्य र अस्वभाविक भनेको छ । अदालतले सन् २०१६ मा करिब १ खर्ब ४३ अर्ब रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरिएको शेयरलाई अत्यन्तै न्यून मूल्यमा किनबेच गरिएको भन्नुलाई नै कानूनको उल्लङ्घनको रुपमा ठहर गरेको हो। सर्वोच्चले आदेशमा भनेको छ, ’शेयर खरीद बिक्री कारोबारको बारेमा विदेशी लगानी तथा प्रविधि हस्तान्तरण ऐन, २०७५ को दफा १९ को अभिलेख राख्ने व्यवस्थासँग आफूलाई अनुमति दिने, नियमन गर्ने विशेष कानूनको रूपमा रहेको दुर सञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ को नियम १५ (१) (ट) को व्यवस्थालाई नजरअन्दाज गर्न मिल्ने देखिएन ।

प्रस्तुत संशोधित ऐ. नियम १५ ( १ ) (ट) तथा नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरण ( अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिको शेयर खरीद बिक्री) विनियमावली, २०७६ को विनियम (१), (३) र विनियम ४ को खण्ड (क) लाई चुनौति दिएको अवस्था पनि रहेको छैन । अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्ति विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडको ८०% शेयर धारण गर्ने शेयरवाला आजियाटा इन्भेष्टमेन् (यु.के.) लिमिटेडले आफ्नो शेयर स्पेक्ट्रलाइट यु.के. लिमिटेडलाई मिति २०८० । ८ । १५ (तदनुसार १ डिसेम्बर २०२३) मा बिक्री गरेको तथ्यमा विवाद देखिदैन । उक्त शेयर कारोवार हुनु अगावै नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरणबाट पूर्व स्वीकृति लिनुपर्नेमा नलिएको, विपक्षीबाट पेस भएको लिखित जवाफमा शेयरधनीको शेयर खरीद बिक्री हुँदा प्राधिकरणबाट स्वीकृति लिनुपर्ने व्यवस्था नै छैन भन्ने जिकिर लिएको र मिति २०८० । ८ । १५ (तदनुसार डिसेम्वर १ सन् २०२३) मा भएको शेयर खरीद बिक्री सम्झौताको सम्बन्धमा मिति २०८०।११।१२ मा मात्र स्वीकृतिको लागि प्राधिकरणमा निवेदन पेस गरेको स्थिति देखिएकाले विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडले दुर सञ्चार ऐन, २०५३, दुर सञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ र नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरण (अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिको शेयर खरीद बिक्री) विनियमावली, २०७६ र अनुमतिपत्रको शर्तसमेत अक्षरशः परिपालना गर्दै पारदर्शी र विधिसम्मत तरिकाले सेवा संचालन गर्नू भनी विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडको नाममा निर्देशनात्मक आदेश जारी गरिदिएको छ ।’

यसरी हेर्दा अब एनसेलको सञ्चालन एनसेल आजियाटाले नै गर्नुपर्नेछ। यसरी हेर्दा सतिसलालले गरेको कारोबार अवैध ठहर भएको छ भने अब ससितलाल एनसेलको अध्यक्षभन्दा पनि कर्मचारी वा अन्य हैसियतमा पुग्ने भएका छन्।

अब सरकारीकरणको बाटो खुला

नेपालको दूरसञ्चार ऐनले निश्वित अवधिपछि निश्चित कानूनी बाटो पुरा नगरेमा टेलिकम कम्पनी नेपाल सरकारको नाममा स्वतः आउने व्यवस्था गरेको छ। जसअनुसार दूरसञ्चार ऐन, २०५३ को दफा ३३ अनुसार ५० प्रतिशतभन्दा बढी विदेशी लगानी भएका दूरसञ्चार कम्पनीहरूको अनुमतिपत्रको २५ वर्षे अवधि समाप्त भएपछि त्यसको स्वामित्व स्वतः नेपाल सरकारमा हस्तान्तरण हुने व्यवस्था गरेको छ ।

एनसेलले १६ भदौ २०६१ मा अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त गरेकाले १५ भदौ २०८६ मा यसको २५ वर्षे अवधि पुरा हुनेछ । जुन अवधिपछि एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्वमा वैध वदलाव नआएमा सरकारीकरणको चरणमा प्रवेश गर्ने निश्वित छ ।

उसोतः एनसेल प्रकरणमा नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआइबी)ले ठगी, आपराधिक विश्वासघात जस्ता विषयमा अनुसन्धान भने गरिरहेको छ। सर्वोच्चले एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व सरकारको नाममा आउने बाटो खुला गरिदिएपनि कानूनी बाटाहरु कसरी अघि बढ्छन्? सरकारी नीति कस्ता बन्छन भन्ने विषयले समेत यो विषयमा थप निर्धारण गर्नेछ ।

अमरेशको सक्रियता

तत्कालीन समयमा स्वतन्त्र रुपमा प्रतिनिधिसभामा निर्वाचित भएका अमरेशकुमार सिंहले एनसेलको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई चुनौती दिदै सर्वोच्चमा रिट दर्ता गराए। अमरेश अहिले राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टीबाट कांग्रेस सभापति गगन थापालाई पराजित गर्दै फेरि सर्लाही निर्वाचन क्षेत्र नम्बर ४ बाट प्रतिनिधिसभा सदस्यमा निर्वाचित भइसकेका छन्।

उनै सिंहले सर्वोच्चमा एनसेल आजियाटा, दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरण, प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालय, ठूला करदाता कार्यालय, कम्पनी रजिष्ट्रार जस्ता धेरै निकायलाई विपक्षी बनाएर रिट दर्ता गराएका थिए। यहि प्रकरणमा सर्वोच्चको फैसलाले एनसेलको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई अवैध ठहर गरेको हो।

निर्णय अब सरकारको हातमा

नेपालमा विदेशी लगानीका सम्बन्धमा अनेक अफवाहहरु फैलिने गर्छन्। कतिपयले एनसेल प्रकरणले नेपालमा ठूला लगानी नआउने भन्दै यसलाई मोड्ने प्रयास समेत गरेको देखिन्छ। सरकारले पनि मध्यम वर्गलाई ठूलो प्रभाव पर्ने गरि काम गरिरहेको बेला विदेशी लगानीलाई नेपालको कानूनको पालना गर्ने र विवादको समाधानका निम्ति सहजीकरणको बाटो खोज्दै काम गर्ने वातावरण सिर्जना गर्नुपर्ने देखिन्छ ।

एनसेल कब्जा गर्ने सतिसलालसहितको टोलीले नै स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति कौडीको भाउमा लिलाम सकारेको घटनाबाटै सरकारले कानूनको पालना गराउने र आवश्यक सहजीकरणसहित दण्ड र पुरस्कारको व्यवस्था गर्न आवश्यक देखिन्छ। तर, सरकारले यस्ता विषयलाई कसरी अघि लैजान्छ भन्ने चासो र केहि शंकाहरु भने देखिन्छन। यद्यपी अब कानूनविपरितका विषयलाई दण्ड र विदेशी लगानीलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्ने गरि काम गर्नुको विकल्प भने देखिन्न ।

articles.title: कोलकाताबाट २४ घण्टामै नेपालमा ढुवानी, व्यवसायी उत्साहित
articles.summary:
मोरङ । उद्घाटन भएको करिब ३ वर्षपछि विराटनगरस्थित एकीकृत जाँच चौकीसम्म कार्गो रेलको सेवा पुनः शुरु भएको छ । पारवहन सन्धीको प्रोटोकल संसोधन पछि विराटनगरको एकीकृत जाँच चौकीस्थित नेपालको कस्टम यार्डसम्म कार्गो रेल आएको हो ।

विराटनगर स्थित एकिकृत जाँच चौकीसम्म कार्गो रेलको सेवा पुनः शुरु भएको छ । तत्कालिन प्रधानमन्त्री पुष्पकमल दाहाल प्रचण्ड र भारतका प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीले २०८० साल जेठ १८ गते उद्घाटन गरेयता कार्गो रेल आउन सकेको थिएन ।

मोरङको नेमुवास्थित स्वस्तिक आयल इण्डष्ट्रिजले मगाएको तोरी बोकेका ४० वटा कन्टेनरसहितको कार्गो रेल नेपाल भंसार यार्डसम्म आएको हो । रेल आएपछि सुनसरी मोरङ औद्योगिक करिडोरका उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरु उत्साहित भएका छन् ।

कार्गो रेलबाट ढुवानी गर्दा ढुवानी लागत २५ देखि ३० प्रतिशत घट्ने, कोलकाता बन्दरगाहबाट विराटनगरसम्म २४ घण्टामा सामान आईपुग्ने र बाटोमा सामान चोरी हुने समस्या निराकरण हुने भएकाले अन्य क्षेत्रका उद्योगहरुसँग प्रतिस्पर्धा गर्न सहज हुने उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरुले बताएका छन् ।

भारत सरकार अन्र्तर्गतको कन्कोर अर्थात कन्टेनर कर्पोरेशन अफ इण्डिया लिमिटेडको कार्गाे रेलबाट सोमवार एनसिवाई अर्थात नेपाल कस्टम यार्ड सम्म मालवाहक रेल आएको हो ।

कन्कोरका प्रतिनिधि संजिव साहले हप्तामा दुई दिन कोलकाताबाट विराटनगरसम्म कार्गो रेल संचालन गर्ने र यसलाई आवश्यकता अनुसार बढाउदै लैजाने जानकारी दिए ।

पारवहन सन्धीको प्रोटोकल संसोधनपछि विराटनगरको एकीकृत जाँच चौकीस्थित नेपाल कस्टम यार्डसम्म कार्गो रेल आएको हो । कार्गो रेल संचालन पछि विराटनगर आएको कन्टेनर खाली फर्कने भएकाले यहाँबाट वस्तु निर्यातमा पनि सहजता आउने उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरुले बताएका छन् ।

articles.title: प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालद्वारा ‘Soirée Francaise’ आयोजना: फ्रान्सेली संस्कृति र जीवनशैलीको अनुभव
articles.summary:
अग्नि ग्रुप अन्तर्गतको प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालले ‘Soirée Française – A Night of French Elegance’ शीर्षकमा एक विशेष 'फ्रेन्च फाइन डाइनिङ' कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न गरेको छ। काठमाडौँस्थित ला टेरास (La Terrasse) मा आयोजना गरिएको उक्त कार्यक्रममा प्युजोका विशिष्ट ग्राहक, व्यावसायिक साझेदार तथा फ्रान्सेली संस्कृतिप्रति आत्मियता राख्ने अतिथिहरूको उपस्थिति रहेको थियो।

कार्यक्रमले फ्रान्सको समृद्ध सांस्कृतिक विरासत र त्यसको प्रेरणादायी भावनालाई सम्मान गर्दै आपसी सम्बन्धलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाउने उद्देश्य राखेको थियो।

विश्वकपमा फ्रान्सेली टोलीको भावनाबाट प्रेरित

सन् २०२६ को फिफा विश्वकपमा फ्रान्सेली टोलीले प्रदर्शन गरेको समर्पण, दृढता, उत्कृष्टता र एकताको भावनाबाट प्रेरित भई यो कार्यक्रम आयोजना गरिएको हो। खेलको नतिजाभन्दा माथि उठेर फ्रान्सेली खेल संस्कृतिको अदम्य भावना र त्यसको विरासतलाई सम्मान गर्नु कार्यक्रमको मुख्य पक्ष थियो। यी मूल्यहरू प्युजो ब्रान्डको दीर्घकालीन पहिचानसँग समेत मेल खाने भएकाले सोही भावनालाई कार्यक्रममा प्रतिबिम्बित गरिएको थियो।

नेटवर्किङ र प्रिमियम जीवनशैलीको अनुभव

कार्यक्रममा सहभागी अतिथिहरूले पेरिस-प्रेरित आकर्षक सजावट तथा आत्मीय वातावरणमा विविध परम्परागत फ्रेन्च परिकारको स्वाद लिँदै नेटवर्किङको अनुभव सँगालेका थिए। प्युजोको फ्रान्सेली सम्पदालाई झल्काउँदै आफ्ना ग्राहकहरूप्रति कृतज्ञता व्यक्त गर्न र नेपालमा प्युजो समुदायसँगको सम्बन्धलाई अझ मजबुत बनाउन यस अवसरले सहयोग पुर्‍याएको कम्पनीले जनाएको छ।

ग्राहक केन्द्रित प्रतिबद्धता

यस अवसरमा प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालका प्रतिनिधिहरूले गुणस्तरीय गतिशीलता (मोबिलिटी) समाधानका साथै ग्राहकलाई अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरको जीवनशैली अनुभव प्रदान गर्ने र विश्वव्यापी रूपमा प्युजोले प्रतिनिधित्व गर्ने मूल्य एवम् परम्परालाई निरन्तर अघि बढाउने प्रतिबद्धता पुनः व्यक्त गरे।

कार्यक्रमको समापन फ्रान्सेली संस्कृति, मित्रता र उत्कृष्टताको साझा भावनाप्रति सम्मान व्यक्त गर्दै ‘टोस्ट’ (Toast) का साथ गरिएको थियो। सहभागीहरूले यस अविस्मरणीय अनुभवले प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपाल र ग्राहकहरूबीचको प्रिमियम सम्बन्धलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाएको विश्वास व्यक्त गरेका छन्

articles.title: राष्ट्रिय इन्जिनियर दिवस घोषणा गर्न इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसनको माग
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपाल इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसनका अध्यक्ष सुवासचन्द्र बरालले प्रत्येक वर्ष साउन ३ गते मनाइने इन्जिनियर दिवसलाई सरकारले औपचारिक रूपमा ‘राष्ट्रिय इन्जिनियर दिवस’ घोषणा गरी सरकारी क्यालेन्डरमा समावेश गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन्।

एसोसियसनको ६४औँ इन्जिनियर दिवस समारोहलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै अध्यक्ष बरालले पूर्वाधार र प्रविधि कुनै पनि राष्ट्रको आर्थिक विकास र समृद्धिको मेरुदण्ड भएको उल्लेख गर्दै इन्जिनियरिङ क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राखेर राज्यले दीर्घकालीन नीति अवलम्बन गर्नुपर्ने बताए।

उनका अनुसार नेपालमा दर्ता भएका करिब एक लाख इन्जिनियरमध्ये करिब ६० प्रतिशत युवा छन्। तर पर्याप्त रोजगारी र अवसरको अभावका कारण ठूलो संख्यामा दक्ष जनशक्ति विदेश पलायन भइरहेको भन्दै उनले यसलाई रोक्न तत्काल प्रभावकारी नीति आवश्यक रहेको बताए।

‘युवा इन्जिनियरहरूको सीप, ज्ञान र दक्षताको उचित उपयोग गर्न राज्य, उद्योग र इन्जिनियरिङ समुदायबीच बलियो सहकार्य आवश्यक छ,’ उनले भने।

बरालले यस वर्षको इन्जिनियर दिवस 'Young Mind and Engineering: Shaping Better Nepal' भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइएको जानकारी दिँदै विकास निर्माणमा संलग्न प्राविधिकहरूले कार्यस्थलमा असुरक्षा, प्रशासनिक झन्झट र अनावश्यक दबाब झेल्नुपरेको गुनासो गरे। यस्तो अवस्थाले विकास आयोजनाको गति नै प्रभावित भएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

उनले प्राविधिकहरूको क्षमताको अधिकतम उपयोग गर्न पुरस्कार र दण्डको स्पष्ट प्रणाली लागू गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता औँल्याए। ऊर्जा, जलस्रोत, कृषि, पर्यटन, सूचना प्रविधि, उद्योग तथा मानव संसाधनलगायत सबै क्षेत्रमा इन्जिनियरहरूको भूमिका निर्णायक रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै बदलिँदो प्रविधिअनुसार सीप विकासमा लगानी बढाउनुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

सरकारसमक्ष एसोसियसनले इन्जिनियरिङ क्षेत्रसँग सम्बन्धित विभिन्न नीतिगत माग पनि अघि सारेको छ।

अध्यक्ष बरालले विकास निर्माणमा खटिने इन्जिनियरका लागि सुरक्षित कार्य वातावरणको कानुनी प्रत्याभूति, रणनीतिक सरकारी निकायको नेतृत्व तहमा प्राविधिक पृष्ठभूमिका इन्जिनियरहरूको प्रतिनिधित्व, छुट्टै इन्जिनियरिङ सेवा आयोग गठन तथा नेपाल इन्जिनियरिङ प्रशिक्षण तथा अनुसन्धान प्रतिष्ठान स्थापना प्रक्रिया तत्काल अघि बढाउन आग्रह गरे।

त्यसैगरी, युवा इन्जिनियरका लागि पर्याप्त रोजगारी सिर्जना, विकास आयोजनाको सुपरभिजन इन्जिनियरबाटै गराउने व्यवस्था, निजी तथा गैरसरकारी क्षेत्रमा कार्यरत इन्जिनियरहरूको न्यूनतम मासिक पारिश्रमिक ३७ हजार १३५ कार्यान्वयन तथा प्राविधिक त्रुटिलाई स्वतः भ्रष्टाचारको कसुर अन्तर्गत नराख्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था गर्न पनि उनले सरकारसँग माग गरे।

अध्यक्ष बरालले नेपाल इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसन इन्जिनियरहरूको पेशागत हकहितको संरक्षण, नवप्रवर्तनको प्रवर्द्धन र राज्यसँग इन्जिनियरिङ समुदायलाई जोड्ने साझा संस्थाका रूपमा निरन्तर सक्रिय रहने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गर्दै सम्पूर्ण इन्जिनियर तथा आर्किटेक्टलाई पेशागत नैतिकता र इमान्दारितालाई सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकतामा राखेर समृद्ध नेपाल निर्माणमा योगदान दिन आह्वान गरे।

articles.title: जेनजी आन्दोलन प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । गत वर्षको भदौ २३ र २४ गते देशमा भएको जेनजी विद्रोह र त्यसक्रममा भएका गम्भीर मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका घटनासम्बन्धी राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघ पुगेको छ ।

नेपालभित्र प्रतिवेदन सार्वजनिक गर्न चौतर्फी माग भइरहेका बेला आयोगले करिब १० हजार पृष्ठ लामो उक्त प्रतिवेदन जेनेभास्थित मानवअधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयमा पेश गरेको छ।

तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री केपी शर्मा ओली र गृहमन्त्री रमेश लेखकसहित उच्च अधिकारीहरूमाथि फौजदारी अनुसन्धानको सिफारिस गरिएको यो प्रतिवेदन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मञ्चमा पुगेसँगै अब सरकारमाथि कूटनीतिक र अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब बढ्ने देखिएको छ ।

गएको भदौ २३–२४ गतेको जेनजी विद्रोहसम्बन्धी राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघीय मानव अधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालय ओएचसीएचआर जेनेभामा पेश भएको छ ।

यो प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि अब सरकारलाई थप दबाब पर्नेछ । जुन १५ देखि जुलाइ ७ सम्म जेनेभामा चलेको ह्युमन राइट काउन्सिलको २४औँ बैठक र ६२ औँ सत्रमा राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगका सदस्य मिहिर ठाकुरले नेपालमा भएको जेनजी विद्रोहको मानवअधिकार अवस्थाका विस्तृत विवरणसहितको प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि सरकारलाई बुझाएको जानकारी दिँदै सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वय गर्नैपर्ने जानकारी गराएका थिए ।

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयले राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगले पेश गरेको प्रतिवेदनलाई नोटमा राखेको छ । सरकारलाई मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि अरु दबाब पर्नेछ । जेनेभा बैठकमा भाग लिन आयोगका सदस्य ठाकुरसँगै आयोगकी उपसचिव माया शर्मा पनि पुगेकी थिइन ।

सरकारमाथि अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब बढाउने रणनीति

आयोगभित्रैका केही अधिकारीहरूका अनुसार सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगर्ने आशंका बढेपछि आयोगले प्रतिवेदन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मञ्चमा पठाएको हो ।

नेपालमै प्रतिवेदन पूर्णरूपमा सार्वजनिक गर्न आग्रह मानव अधिकार आयोगले आग्रह गरे पनि त्यो सम्भव नभएको बताउने गरेकाले पनि अब जेनेभाबाटै थप प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढ्न सक्ने अवस्था बनेको छ ।

प्रतिवेदनमा को–कोमाथि अनुसन्धान सिफारिस ?

जेनजी आन्दोलनमा भएको दमन, गोली प्रहार, सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगजनी तथा विध्वंसका घटनाबारे आयेगको प्रतिवेदन करिब १० हजार पृष्ठको छ । तर आयोगले प्रतिवेदनको केही अंश मात्रै सार्वजनिक गरेको थियो ।

उक्त प्रतिवेदनमा तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री केपी शर्मा ओली, तत्कालीन गृहमन्त्री रमेश लेखक, तत्कालीन सञ्चारमन्त्री पृथ्वी सुब्बा गुरुङ, तत्कालीन प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक चन्द्रकुवेर खापुङ लगायतमाथि फौजदारी अनुसन्धान अघि बढाउन सिफारिस गरिएको छ ।

यसैगरी आन्दोलनका क्रममा भएको विध्वंसमा कलाकार, पत्रकार, इन्फ्लुएन्सर तथा हाल संसद् र सरकारमा रहेका केही व्यक्तिहरूमाथि पनि थप अनुसन्धान गर्न आयोगले सिफारिस गरेको छ ।

आन्दोलनका घटनाबारे आयोगको निष्कर्ष

पूर्ण प्रतिवेदनमा भदौ २३ देखि २६ सम्मका घटना समेटिएका छन् । कसले कोसँग संवाद ग¥यो ?के–के कुरा भयो ? सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगो लगाउनेसम्ममा कसको योजना थियो भन्ने समेटिएका छन् ।

भीड कसरी उग्र बन्यो, सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगजनी गर्ने योजना कसरी बनेको थियो भन्ने विवरण पनि प्रतिवेदनमा समावेश छ । आयोगले अनुसन्धानका लागि आवश्यक केही प्रमाण, विशेषगरी गोलीका अवशेष बुलेट संकलन गर्न नसकिएको स्वीकार गरेको छ ।

ओली–लेखकले नै मागेका छन्, प्रतिवेदनको प्रतिलिपि

आयोगको पूर्ण प्रतिवेदन सार्वजनिक गर्न माग भइरहँदा फौजदारी अनुसन्धान अघि बढाउन सिफारिस गरिएका पूर्व प्रधानमन्त्री एवम् एमाले अध्यक्ष ओली, पूर्व गृहमन्त्री एवम् कांग्रेस नेता रमेश लेखक, पूर्व सञ्चार मन्त्री पृथ्वी सुब्बा गुरुङले प्रतिवेदनमाथि प्रश्न उठाउँदै आयोगसमक्ष निवेदन दर्ता गराएका छन् ।

प्रतिवेदनको केही अंश झिकिएको र केही अंश थपिएको आशंकापछि उनीहरुले प्रतिवेदन माग गरेका हुन् । ओलीको तर्फबाट छानबिन तथा अनुसन्धान प्रतिवेदन माग गर्दै एमाले नेता महेश बर्तौलाले असार १२ गते आयोगमा निवेदन दर्ता गराएका थिए ।

ओलीले आयोगको बैठकको निर्णय नम्बर १७७ को प्रमाणित प्रतिलिपि, लिली थापा नेतृत्वको समितिले आयोगमा पेश गरेको प्रतिवेदनको प्रतिलिपि, प्रतिवेदनमा थपघट गरिएको अंश र थपघट गर्नुको कारणसमेत माग गरेका छन् ।

यस्तै, रास्वपा सभापति रवि लामिछानेलाई कारागारबाट बाहिर निकाल्न गएको आरोप लागेका सांसद दीपक बोहोराले पनि आयोगमा निवेदन दिएका थिए । आयोगले भनेको समयमा आफू अस्पतालमा रहेको उनको दलिल छ ।

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयमा प्रतिवेदन पेश भएपछि के हुन्छ ?

संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघको मानवअधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयले अब चार चरणमा प्रक्रिया अघि बढाउँछ ।

पहिलो चरण : अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय अभिलेखः–

प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघको आधिकारिक अभिलेखमा दर्ता हुन्छ । यसले नेपालमा मानव अधिकार उल्लंघन भएको दाबी अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय निगरानीमा प्रवेश गर्छ ।

दोस्रो चरण : प्रश्न र स्पष्टीकरणः–

मानव अधिकार परिषद्का सदस्य राष्ट्रहरूले नेपाल सरकारसँग स्पष्टीकरण माग्न सक्छन् ।

तेस्रो चरण : सिफारिसः–

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालय वा विशेष प्रतिवेदकहरूले नेपाललाई अनुसन्धान, पीडितलाई क्षतिपूर्ति वा जिम्मेवार व्यक्तिमाथि कारबाही गर्न सिफारिस गर्न सक्छन् ।

चौथो चरण : निगरानीः–

नेपालले ती सिफारिस कार्यान्वयन ग¥यो कि गरेन भनेर आगामी सत्रहरूमा पुनःसमीक्षा हुन्छ ।

जेनजी प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनमा दबाब

जेनजी आन्दोलनको प्रतिवेदन अब नेपालको आन्तरिक राजनीतिक विवाद मात्र रहेन, अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मानव अधिकार बहसको विषय बनेको छ । मानव अधिकार परिषद्को ६२औँ सत्रमा यसबारे औपचारिक जानकारी प्रस्तुत भइसकेकाले नेपाल सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगरेमा आगामी सत्रहरूमा थप प्रश्न उठ्न सक्छन् ।

यद्यपी प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगरेकै कारण कुनै देशलाई तुरुन्त प्रतिबन्ध भने लाग्दैन ।तर अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय आलोचना बढ्छ । मानव अधिकार सम्बन्धी वार्षिक प्रतिवेदनमा नकारात्मक उल्लेख हुन्छ । यसको असरले वैदेशिक सहायता र विकास साझेदारहरूको दबाब बढ्न सक्छ ।

त्यस्तै, विशेष प्रतिवेदक वा अनुसन्धान टोली पठाउने सम्भावना पनि रहन्छ। नेपालमा विगतमा द्वन्द्वकालीन मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनका विषयमा संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघले पटक–पटक चासो व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

यस्ता घटनामा कुन कुन देशलाई प्रतिबन्ध लागेको छ ?

मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनका आधारमा विभिन्न देशहरूमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको उदाहरणहरु छन् । म्यानमारमा सैन्य दमन र मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनको घटनामा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको छ भने इरानमा प्रदर्शनकारीमाथि दमन गरेको भन्दै मानवअधिकार उल्लंघन भएको निश्कर्षमा प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको छ।

त्यस्तै मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका घटना छानबिन गरेर कारवाही नगरेका कारण बेलारुस, गृहयुद्ध र मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका कारण सिरिया लगायतका देश प्रतिबन्धमा परेका छन् ।

articles.title: RSP to appoint leadership in phases after Shah camp misses deadline
articles.summary:
Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Chairman Rabi Lamichhane is preparing to nominate a limited number of central committee members and office bearers after Prime Minister Balendra Shah's camp failed to submit its recommendations for appointments ahead of the party's central committee meeting.

The ruling party's central committee is scheduled to meet at 11am on Wednesday, with organisational management and nominations listed as one of the agendas of the meeting. Under the party statute, the chairman can nominate 51 central committee members, subject to endorsement by the central committee.

RSP General Secretary Bipin Acharya said the meeting would make the first round of appointments, although the exact number had yet to be decided.

"The central committee meeting will make the first phase of nominations for central committee members and office bearers. It is not possible to say exactly how many will be nominated. That is why nominations have been included in the meeting agenda," said Acharya.

Party leaders had earlier expected to settle the remaining appointments after the first general convention held in Bharatpur, Chitwan, from June 21 to 26. Newly elected office bearers and central committee members took their oath in Kathmandu on July 1, when discussions were also held on filling the remaining nominated positions.

However, leaders close to Shah said the prime minister's side had not finalised its recommendations. A central committee member close to Shah said discussions on who should be nominated to the central committee and office-bearer positions were still incomplete.

"As of Monday evening, we have not finalised our recommendations for the central committee and office-bearer positions. The prime minister has also been occupied with government responsibilities," the leader said. "Before the central committee meeting, there will probably be further discussions with the chairman so that nominations are in keeping with the spirit of integration. Looking at the preparations, it does not appear that all 51 central committee members and the remaining office bearers will be appointed in one go."

Another central committee member said Lamichhane had concluded that appointments should proceed in different phases because consultations on balancing representation and integrating different groups within the party were still under way.

"The issue of integration has not yet been settled. There has not been sufficient dialogue. Therefore, the chairman believes that appointing some central committee members and office bearers now will allow the party's work to move forward," the leader said.

Besides nominations, Wednesday's meeting will review the party's first general convention, discuss organisational procedures requiring revision after amendments to the party statute, approve future campaigns and programmes, and consider other organisational matters.

Acharya said a thorough review of the convention was necessary to improve future party events.

"We need a critical review of the convention so that the party's future course becomes stronger. We have already apologised for technical and management shortcomings during the convention. As the statute has been amended, several procedures also need to be drafted or revised," he said.

The RSP's first general convention formally restructured the party's leadership and incorporated provisions recognising the post of senior leader. Shah, who joined the party after signing a seven-point agreement with Lamichhane on December 28, 2025, is expected to be formally inducted into the central leadership through nomination before being appointed senior leader.

Party leaders said Shah would first be nominated as a central committee member before assuming the senior leader's role.

Eleven office bearer positions remain vacant, including one vice-chairperson, one general secretary, two joint general secretaries, one spokesperson, three deputy spokespersons, one treasurer and two deputy treasurers. The party statute requires inclusive representation in these appointments, including at least four women and two representatives from marginalised communities such as indigenous nationalities, Madhesis, Dalits, Tharus, Muslims and other minority groups.

articles.title: New land bank procedure aims to revive unused plots, but challenges persist
articles.summary:
The federal government has introduced a land bank system to bring unused private land and vacant plots into productive use through local government.

The initiative aims to enforce land-use classification provisions and increase productivity by ensuring the maximum utilisation of land resources. Under the system, local units will establish land banks to bring privately owned land that is unused or underutilised into use through specific conditions and incentives.

Under the arrangement, local units will issue notices inviting landowners who wish to make their land available through the land bank. Landowners must submit applications containing details such as ownership status, plot number, land area and the period for which they are willing to allow the land to be used.

To establish and operate land banks at every local unit, the government has introduced the Land Bank (Establishment and Operation) Procedure, 2026, in line with the Land Use Act, 2019 and the Land Use (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2025.

The federal Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives, Federal Affairs and General Administration has approved the procedure and circulated it to all local units. The government has also urged people to use the new arrangement through their respective local units.

The Ministry of Land Management said local units do not need to prepare separate procedures as the federal government has already issued the framework. However, Section 21(1) of the Land Use Act, 2019 requires local units seeking to establish land banks to obtain approval from the federal ministry.

“Local units wishing to establish land banks must submit a copy of the executive decision to the ministry,” the procedure states. “The ministry’s division responsible for land use will examine the request as necessary and recommend the establishment of the land bank.”

The procedure adds that local units must establish a land section with the required infrastructure to operate a land bank. The section will identify private land within its jurisdiction that is unused, cannot be utilised by landowners or has remained vacant for other reasons, and prepare details of such land.

After receiving approval to operate a land bank, local units must form a land bank operation committee as required under Rule 13A(2) of the regulations.

The committee will be headed by the mayor of a municipality, chairperson of a rural municipality or a designated executive member. The chief administrative officer of the local unit will serve as a member, while the head of the section responsible for land-related affairs will serve as the member secretary.

The procedure requires local units to open a separate account for the land bank. Deposits made by land users, returns paid by users for using the land and service fees collected from landowners must be deposited into the account.

The account will also include grants provided by the federal, provincial and local governments, as well as other funds allocated by the local executive.

The funds can be used to pay returns owed to depositors, purchase machinery and office supplies required for the land bank, cover expenses incurred during field inspections and provide incentive allowances to employees assigned to operate the land bank.

The procedure also allows multiple local units to jointly operate a land bank. For this, the local units must sign a written agreement specifying the location of the joint land bank’s secretariat, the person responsible as member secretary, the official authorised to sign agreements on behalf of the joint land bank when leasing land in and out, the method for managing income and expenditure from the joint land bank fund, and responsibility for auditing the land bank’s accounts.

The land section must maintain a land bank registration register and record details of land submitted by owners. Before accepting land into the bank, the section must verify that there are no disputes over ownership, including joint ownership or tenancy rights. In cases involving tenanted land, consent from the tenant must also be obtained.

The section must also verify that the plot number, area and boundaries of the land are accurate, that the land is not under any restriction and that it can be used according to the land-use classification. If necessary, technical officials must conduct field inspections and submit a report assessing whether the land is suitable for use.

If the land is found unsuitable, the section must inform the landowner. If it is deemed suitable, the section must submit details of the land, along with the expected returns sought by the landowner, to the operation committee for approval to accept it into the land bank.

The operations committee can either approve or reject the proposal. If approved, the landowner and the section must sign an agreement within seven days. After the agreement is signed, the land must be recorded in the land deposit register and listed as available for use.

The land section must then publish a notice seeking applications from those interested in using land listed with the land bank. The notice must include details of the available land and allow applicants 15 days to submit requests.

Applications received from potential users must be registered in the land bank register. Before providing land through the bank, authorities must consider factors including the return proposed by the landowner, views of adjoining landowners, the practicality of the proposed use, potential for employment generation and environmental suitability.

The land section must prepare a priority list for allocating land and obtain approval from the local executive. For applications received from individuals seeking land use, the section must submit proposals to the operation committee within seven days after the application deadline, and the committee must decide whether to provide the land.

The committee must clearly specify the annual return that the user will be required to pay. The procedure states that individuals seeking to use land through the bank must deposit 10 percent of the annual return amount as security.

After permission is granted to use the land, the land section must write to the Land Revenue Office to restrict the property, preventing the landowner from selling, transferring ownership or registering a mortgage on it.

The procedure allows the restriction to be lifted if the landowner takes back the land with the consent of the user, if the local government withdraws the land it had provided for use, or if the user does not renew the agreement after the usage period expires.

If no one applies to use land listed with the land bank, the land bank can invite applications from cooperatives, groups or companies, according to the procedure. If a local unit decides to use the land itself, it must make the land available to interested target groups within its jurisdiction to use it according to specified conditions.

Local units must prepare a priority list of target groups, including landless and squatter communities, Dalit families owning less than five kattha of land (one kattha equals 0.03386 hectares), freed Kamaiya or freed Haliya families, families of martyrs, families holding government-issued identity cards for access to state benefits, and small-scale farmers.

If the user does not renew the agreement after the land-use period expires, the land will automatically be considered returned to the owner. If either party wants to return or take back the land before the agreement ends, both parties must inform the operation committee at least three months in advance. The procedure states that land returned after use must be handed back in the same condition in which it was received.

However, if any structure has been built on the land and the landowner has no objection to keeping it, the user will not be required to demolish and remove the structure.

The return received by landowners will be determined according to the agreement signed with the local unit. The procedure states that the land bank may charge landowners a service fee of no more than 10 percent of the return amount for taking responsibility for the land and making it available for use.

The local unit must deposit the remaining amount into the landowner’s bank account after deducting the service fee payable to the land bank.

Users must deposit 10 percent of the annual payment amount as a security deposit at the time of signing the agreement and pay the remaining amount according to the terms of the agreement. If users fail to pay the amount owed to the land bank, the local unit can recover it as government arrears.

The procedure also defines the rights and responsibilities of landowners and users.

Under the rights and responsibilities of landowners, the procedure states that ownership and legal rights over the land will remain with the landowner throughout the agreement period. Landowners must continue paying land revenue and property taxes payable to the government, must not interfere during the agreement period and cannot sell the land without the user’s consent.

Users, meanwhile, must use the land only for the specified purpose, protect the boundaries, existing infrastructure and soil fertility, and cannot allow anyone else to use the land.

If the boundary walls, embankments or borders of the land are damaged due to negligence or any other reason during the period of use, the user must repair the damage and return the land to its original condition before handing it back.

Users are also prohibited from changing the condition or structure of the land without the landowner’s approval.

The procedure requires local units to provide seeds, fertilisers, technical support and cash grants under their regular production-enhancement programmes to individuals, organisations or companies using vacant land through the land bank.

While providing grants, local units must prioritise activities such as grain production, vegetable farming, cash crops, fish farming, livestock and poultry farming, fruit cultivation, purchasing and processing local products, and other businesses.

If disputes arise between land users, land banks and landowners regarding land use or the payment and receipt of returns, the operation committee must resolve them based on the terms of the agreement, according to the procedure.

If a user is unable to fully utilise land because of a legal dispute that existed before the land was handed over for use, the landowner will be responsible for paying compensation through the land bank.

Similarly, if users damage embankments, boundary walls or land borders due to negligence or any other reason during the period of use, they must pay compensation for the damage.

The procedure states that users will not be held responsible for damage caused by natural disasters. The amount of compensation in such cases will be determined by the local unit.

Although the federal government approved and implemented the procedure in 2026, some local units had already introduced their own land bank procedures under the Local Government Operation Act, 2017. However, these initiatives have not yet been effectively implemented.

Rupa Rural Municipality in Kaski, Modi Rural Municipality in Parbat, Gulmi Darbar Rural Municipality in Gulmi and Kaligandaki Rural Municipality in Syangja introduced land bank-related procedures as early as 2020.

Similarly, Machhapuchchhre Rural Municipality introduced such procedures in 2023, Resunga Municipality in Gulmi and Bhanu Municipality in Tanahun introduced them in 2024, and Phikkal Rural Municipality in Sindhuli also introduced a land bank procedure in 2026. However, implementation remains limited.

Parbati Sunuwar, chairperson of Phikkal Rural Municipality, said the local unit has already introduced the Land Bank (Establishment and Operation) Procedure, 2026 and has begun issuing notices inviting both landowners willing to lease out land and individuals or organisations seeking land for lease.

“We have fixed rental rates based on the lease period. We have also informed the federal government that we have already prepared the procedure,” she said.

Sunuwar added that the rural municipality has also been providing a subsidy of Rs2,500 per ropani (one ropani equals 0.0509 hectares) to those cultivating vacant land. The programme, which started last year, has been continued this year as well, she said.

Gulmi Darbar Rural Municipality introduced its land bank procedure and issued a public notice in 2020. However, no landowners have come forward to make their vacant land available for use, said Tara Thapa Dhenga, vice-chairperson of the rural municipality.

“We have been issuing notices for the past three or four years asking landowners with unused land to make it available for use, but nobody has shown interest,” she said.

Rupa Rural Municipality has also prepared the Land Bank Operation Procedure, 2020. However, vice-chairperson Lal Subba Gurung said the local unit has faced difficulties because the federal land-use regulations did not provide detailed provisions on land banks.

Although the rural municipality introduced the procedure and began preparations in 2020, it could not implement the programme because the federal government had not included detailed rules on land banks, said the municipality chair, Nawaraj Ojha.

“We prepared the procedure, established the land bank, and even issued notices, but the land was not placed under restriction,” he said. “The Land Revenue Office said it could not restrict transactions unless the federal government issued clear instructions. We had already completed the process of taking and providing land on lease.”

The government had announced the establishment of land banks across the country in the fiscal year 2020-21 to bring vacant and unused private land into productive use.

The announcement came as the number of privately owned plots lying unused continued to rise. The government said such land would be commercially utilised to increase productivity. The policy and programme for fiscal year 2020-21 stated that land bank units would be established in 300 local units through joint investment by the federal, provincial and local governments.

The Land Use Act, 2019, also included provisions related to land banks under Section 21.

However, the Land Use Regulations issued on June 6, 2022, did not include provisions on land banks. Although the concept was included in the Act, it was absent from the regulations.

The federal government later incorporated land banks into the Land Use (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2025.

Ganesh Bhatta, spokesperson for the Ministry of Land Management, said local units can operate land banks only after obtaining approval from the federal government.

“One local unit had sought approval before the procedure was approved,” he said. “But since our procedure had not been approved at that time, approval was not granted. Since then, no local unit has sought approval.”

articles.title: Rights groups stand by impeachment allegations. Government pushes back
articles.summary:
Rumours of an impending impeachment motion against Supreme Court justices have spilled into the international arena, turning an internal judicial dispute into a high-stakes confrontation.

The escalating controversy follows a joint statement issued on Friday by three prominent global human rights organisations—Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International, and the International Commission of Jurists—claiming they received credible information that three apex court justices were being pressured to resign under threat of impeachment.

However, they have not made public the reports or any other evidence on which they based their claims. Talking to Kantipur, a representative of one of the organisations said that the joint statement had been issued on the basis of credible information they had received, but declined to disclose the source of that information or provide any further details.

Nirajan Thapaliya, Director of Amnesty International Nepal, said that the three organisations had issued their statement not on the basis of any written report but on information received from credible and highly reliable sources. He added that they continue to stand by their position.

"We do not have any report provided by anyone. However, we issued this statement on the basis of information we received from credible and highly reliable sources," said Thapaliya.

The allegations have drawn sharp rejections from the government and the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP). Authorities insisted that no such coercion or impeachment plans were ever conceived.

Minister for Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Sobita Gautam dismissed the charges, arguing that the executive branch would never cross such constitutional boundaries. "As a student of law, I am exceptionally clear about the limits of government power and the delicate sensitivity required when dealing with the judiciary," said Gautam. She further challenged the international organisations to substantiate their claims publicly. "Those who issued the statement must verify their claims. Making mere accusations is insufficient."

Echoing her stance, RSP General Secretary Bipin Acharya labeled the charges baseless, stating that the governing party had not even contemplated initiating an impeachment motion against any justices.

Despite official denials, the international involvement has intensified scrutiny over internal Supreme Court dynamics. Observers note that the friction within the judiciary worsened after the Constitutional Council recommended Justice Manoj Sharma—the fourth senior justice—for appointment as Chief Justice, bypassing established convention of seniority. Senior-most Justice Sapana Pradhan Malla publicly opposed the break with tradition. Malla subsequently took leave for several weeks before returning to his judicial responsibilities.

Legal experts and former jurists warn that the ongoing public hostility between international watchdogs and the government poses a grave threat to the judicial system.

Former Supreme Court Justice Ishwar Prasad Khatiwada took to social media to reflect on the situation, raising critical questions regarding the veracity of the claims. Khatiwada noted that while everyone hopes the allegations mentioned by the three rights groups are proven false, baseless accusations or real threats both severely undermine judicial dignity. Speaking later, Khatiwada emphasised that once serious allegations are raised in the public domain, clear and transparent answers must follow to restore public trust.

Former Supreme Court Justice Top Bahadur Singh, who currently serves as the president of the Former Judges Forum, warned that external political pressure dismantles the foundational principles of a fair trial. "When a justice sits on the bench to dispense justice, they must sit free from both external pressure and improper influence," said Singh. "When rumours circulate outside that an impeachment motion is being prepared or that a resignation is being demanded, it creates direct pressure on the fair execution of justice. Judges cannot perform their duties impartially under such circumstances."

Within the Supreme Court, serving justices acknowledged that impeachment talk had been circulating through informal conversations for weeks. Out of four sitting justices interviewed by Kantipur, three confirmed hearing the rumours, describing such political maneuvering as destructive to the legal system.

"Punitive measures based on an objective evaluation of judicial performance are acceptable, but actions driven by political prejudice will destroy the judiciary," a sitting Supreme Court justice said on condition of anonymity. "Today, a specific justice may be targeted, but this dangerous precedent will spare no one in the future. The direct victim of this exercise will be the delivery of justice."

Another sitting justice expressed deep concern that the judiciary might relapse into past crises, recalling previous impeachment motions against former chief justices Sushila Karki and Cholendra Shamsher Rana.

Political parties are alleged to be utilising impeachment powers as a tool to intimidate the bench rather than enforce accountability. The 2017 impeachment motion against Sushila Karki was eventually withdrawn following public outrage, while the 2022 motion against Cholendra Shamsher Rana effectively sidelined him until his retirement without ever reaching a definitive parliamentary vote.

"If a justice lacks competence or commits a serious crime, they must not be granted immunity. However, if justices are removed simply because the government does not receive favorable rulings or due to political bias, where does judicial independence remain?” said another sitting justice. "The government must not entangle itself in such disputes. The executive must do its job and allow the judiciary to function independently; both branches must strictly respect their constitutional boundaries."

Defending the intervention of global watchdogs, senior advocate Raju Chapagai noted that international human rights institutions operate under specific investigative methodologies. Chapagai, a former legal advisor to the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), said the primary objective of such organisations is to safeguard judicial integrity.

"Rather than demanding evidence regarding why these three institutions issued the statement, the government must understand the underlying message in a timely manner," said Chapagai. "The independence of the judiciary is not merely a domestic matter. It is an international concern."

Under Article 101(2) of the Constitution of Nepal, one-fourth of the House of Representatives can file an impeachment motion against the Chief Justice or Supreme Court justices on grounds of serious constitutional violations, incompetence, or gross misconduct. The motion can be endorsed with a two-thirds majority.

Given the ruling party’s strong parliamentary strength (182 seats in 275-member House of Representatives), the government commands the numbers required to register and pass such a motion. However, legal experts maintain that using extraordinary constitutional powers as political leverage threatens the bedrock of constitutional democracy.

articles.title: Coach behind Sunmaya Budha’s rise sees Nepal as ultra-running’s next powerhouse
articles.summary:
“Nepal, you do not want to lose these athletes.”

This warning comes from Andy DuBois, one of the world’s premier ultra-trail running coaches.

DuBois hails from Australia and is a former elite trail runner himself. He won the gruelling Hardmoors 110-mile (177-kilometre) ultramarathon in 2010, completing the distance in 22:38:00.

DuBois, however, isn’t just an elite endurance coach. He is the world’s go-to expert on using technology to measure a runner’s true effort. Just as cyclists use power metres on their bikes, trail runners now use sensors to measure “power”, or the exact amount of energy their muscles pump out in real time. When Stryd, the world’s leading maker of these running devices, needs expert advice on how energy works on steep mountain trails, they reach out to DuBois. After all, DuBois is the pioneer who turned raw data into a winning strategy on the dirt.

Alongside helping runners from all around the world, DuBois, of late, has also been a major mastermind behind the accolades of Nepali trail runners—including Sunmaya Budha, who broke an 11-year-old record when she won the Lavaredo Ultra Trail 120K in Italy on June 27.

“Coaching Nepali runners has been fascinating because they break stereotypes and push past what we consider normal human capacity,” DuBois told the Post recently over a call from Australia. “Sunmaya is, by far, the best athlete I have ever trained. She takes into account every basic detail required while running for hours.”

DuBois was amazed by Budha’s comeback in the Dolomites. Budha was eight minutes behind Australia’s Lucy Bartholomew with 18 kilometres remaining. But Budha reached the finish line first, and that too, a minute and 41 seconds ahead of Bartholomew.

In a blog, DuBois has explained how Budha went on to win the race in Italy by going past human limits.

“She looks so quiet and calm off the trails,” DuBois added. “But once she puts on a race bib and starts a race, she is an absolute monster—a beast.”

DuBois is convinced that the same fierce beast resides inside scores of Nepali runners.

Currently, the Australian coaches three Nepalis—Sunmaya, her sister Ram Maya, and Man Kumar Roka Magar—while closely tracking the performances and development of others on the domestic circuit.

“There are trails everywhere in Nepal,” DuBois said. “Nepali runners are born and raised in unforgiving terrain and at high altitudes—the exact environment runners around the world spend thousands of dollars seeking out, but rarely get. You have got all the raw ingredients right there.”

He added, “There are many big fish in this small pond.”

Having coached the national trail-running team of the Philippines, the Australian coach suggests Nepal could draw valuable lessons from the island nation’s recent sporting push.

“The Philippines is producing many exceptional trail runners recently because the state is actively investing in the sport,” DuBois explained. “But if you compare the natural conditions of the Philippines with Nepal, this mountainous country has the capacity to do far better.”

At the same time, DuBois offers a pragmatic perspective. He acknowledges that at a time when even far wealthier nations have yet to fully prioritise this gruelling and adventurous sport, expecting massive state intervention from Nepal right away might be unrealistic.

“Trail running is still a niche sport globally,” he noted. “So it is understandable that a developing nation like Nepal hasn’t poured its resources into trail running yet.”

However, DuBois suggests that Nepal can get a fascinating return if it invests in trail running.

“As I said before, Nepal is a perfect breeding ground for trail runners. Nepal could also become a major hub for the world’s premier races,” DuBois said. “Trail runners globally would jump at the chance to train in the ultimate high-altitude environment at a fraction of the cost of visiting the European Alps or the American Rockies.”

DuBois praised the organisation of some of the toughest races in Nepal, such as the Everest Marathon and Manaslu Trail Race. “I have been to Nepal twice till now—in 2001 and 2025,” he said. “And the mountains and the trails there have left me awestruck.”

What amazed DuBois—who has trekked to Annapurna, Pikey Peak and Gokyo Lake in Nepal—more during his time trekking in the mountains of Nepal was the potters.

“They carry kilograms of weight and walk faster than normal individuals,” he said. “They do not earn much every day by carrying those weights and taking such huge risks. If they start running, which will not be a hard change in job for them, they can earn good money at once alongside fame and recognition.

“Yes, that makes total sense,” DuBois responded when shown the story of Arjun Kulung Rai, an Everest porter-turned-trail runner. Rai had recalled feeling as if he was flying when he ran for the first time without a heavy load on his back during the 2013 Everest Marathon—where he finished sixth. Today, Rai is recognised as one of Nepal’s premier ultra-trail athletes, winning races all around the world.

But DuBois clarifies that the advantage of having been brought up in the difficult terrain and high altitudes of Nepal cannot ensure that Nepali runners excel in the world.

“Yes, Nepali runners have it in their genes—to run at high altitudes without any problems,” he continued. “Yet, it is not sufficient to defeat better-trained and well-prepared runners around the world. It is because they need to run continuously for hours and hundreds of kilometres.”

And what does DuBois suggest? That Nepal should produce not only runners but coaches too.

“There are no proper and well-trained coaches in Nepal while the number of runners is increasing,” he said. “Who is going to help these athletes understand the technicalities and become the best in the world?”

Sunmaya Budha was scouted by Ryan Scott Blair of Asia Pacific Adventure-Athletes and helped get sponsorship from Kailas FUGA, a leading trail running brand, in 2024. It was only after this sponsorship that Budha was able to afford the coaching of DuBois.

DuBois recalled his initial coaching days with Sunmaya as troublesome. “She did not have the necessary equipment that could track her training results because those were expensive. But after the sponsorship, she had a watch and other equipment through which I could analyse her results and assign different training regimens.”

Budha widely praises DuBois, who joined her around four months before her race at the 99.1-km UTMB Mont Blanc 2022-CCC [Courmayeur–Champex–Chamonix]. Budha was then recovering from an Achilles injury. And Budha finished second at the race in August 2022.

“Andy has been a prolific coach. He is the best in the world,” Budha told the Post at the Tribhuvan International Airport after arriving from the win in Italy on June 30. “I am getting better and better through his training. It is not easy to get a coach like Andy. We are lucky.”

DuBois, however, argued that Budha has not been able to unlock her full potential yet.

“Sunmaya trains at her hometown in Jumla. Environment-wise it is a great place to train,” DuBois said. “But from what I have heard, there are not even basic services there. How will she manage her diet? Where will she seek treatment in cases of injury? Does she have access to a physiotherapist there?”

But Jumla has its benefits, DuBois said. “Nepali runners love their village and family. That is how they keep up with the pressure of not having sufficient support from the authorities. Imagine them with proper support.”

This is specifically why DuBois stresses that while Nepali trail runners already possess all the “raw ingredients,” what they desperately need now is structured, long-term support.

“I can see Nepal becoming both the ultimate destination for the world’s top races and a producer of elite trail runners capable of dominating the sport globally,” DuBois said. “But it cannot happen overnight. The state needs to have a long-term plan that spans at least over a decade. You start finding talents now, nurture them and then bring them to the world stage and dominate it.”

For now, DuBois plans to see his runners reach the pinnacle of trail running.

“Once Sunmaya wins the UTMB’s biggest races, I will be glad,” DuBois added. “I can see Ram Maya and Man Kumar in the same queue. There is also a plan to include a couple of more emerging Nepali runners in my coaching. Nepal could always win team competitions in trail running and break course records all around the world. It is rare to find such athletes who push that hard, and that too without proper financial and motivational support from the state.”

According to DuBois, the peak age for trail runners is 35 to 45. “While Nepal is amazed with Sunmaya now, she still has a lot to give. And I hope the country will be ready when she and other Nepali runners become the best in the world in the next few years.”

DuBois also shared that he plans to visit Nepal in the next few months. “I would be more than happy to meet Nepali authorities then and make them understand how great athletes the country has and how beneficial it will be for Nepal to invest in trail running.”

articles.title: Nepal’s exam leak is about much more than one WhatsApp group
articles.summary:
The integrity of higher education in Nepal faced a digital betrayal on Friday. Within five minutes of the commencement of the Tribhuvan University’s Master of Business Studies (MBS) first-semester examination for ‘Organisational Behaviour’, the question paper was circulating on a WhatsApp group. A teacher known online as ‘Sulav Sir’, later identified as Sandip Singh, shared the paper and subsequently provided a 16-page handwritten solution while the test was still underway. This brazen act of academic fraud allowed at least 35 active members in a group of over 1,000 to discuss answers in real-time.

Friday’s paper leak is not an isolated case but rather a symptom of a recurring and systemic issue that has plagued Nepal for decades. From the Secondary Education Examination leaks in 2019 to the cancelled MBBS entrance exams in 2014, the history of examination compromises in Nepal is a long and shameful record.

The leak of an examination paper is a blow to the entire student community. For thousands of candidates, these examinations are the culmination of years of study and financial sacrifice by their families. A paper leak shatters the mental health of students by causing stress and anxiety. In many cases, the sudden loss of a fair opportunity drives students toward clinical depression. Families also suffer financial losses from money spent on examination fees, coaching and travel. Honest students lose their motivation to study.

In this context, the response from Education Minister Sasmit Pokharel has been a welcome departure from the usual administrative inertia. He ordered the Nepal Police leadership to conduct a swift, round-the-clock investigation. This rapid coordination led to the arrest of five suspects by the Central Investigation Bureau (CIB) within 24 hours of the incident. Only one remains in custody now. Such swift action is rare in Nepal, where masterminds of past academic rackets have often avoided investigation.

Nepal can draw critical lessons from the recent chaos in neighbouring India. Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following weeks of mass youth demonstrations organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) after the NEET-UG 2026 medical entrance exam was compromised. The Indian government’s initial hesitation and delay in taking high-level accountability only served to fuel public fury and destroy trust in national testing bodies. Nepal must avoid this trajectory by maintaining absolute transparency. The university must establish a clear policy on what constitutes a compromising threshold for an examination.

The current demand for immediate resignation of Minister Pokharel is illogical. Political figures, such as UML leader Mahesh Basnet, are calling for the Minister to step down by citing the moral precedent set in India. This demand is misplaced. Unlike the situation in India where the government hesitated, Pokharel has driven a crackdown on the perpetrators. Preliminary findings indicate that the leak was carried out by a private teacher, not an internal employee of Tribhuvan University. A minister should not be forced out because of the rogue actions of an individual outside the university’s direct payroll. Basnet is simply trying to politicise a serious academic crisis for partisan gain.

For now, the government must set a good precedent by going to the root of this incident. Swift action must be taken not just against individuals but against the structural flaws that allow these leaks to recur. Growing commercialisation of education is a primary driver of these scandals. Many institutions now care more about artificially inflating results than they do about the quality of their students. Political patronage has often protected these academic syndicates in the past, leading to a culture of impunity.

The government must ensure that digital security of examination halls becomes a priority. This includes enforcing absolute bans on personal smart devices in examination halls and utilising signal jamming. The current investigation by the CIB must be fast-tracked to ensure that perpetrators face immediate legal consequences. Nepal needs a system that treats academic merit as sacred. Only by addressing the root causes and ignoring political theatre can the university regain its credibility.

articles.title: Absent MPs: A growing concern for democracy
articles.summary:
It was a pedestrian morning. A few people were sitting in front of a tea shop in Pipara Bazaar, Rautahat. A newspaper was open, hands still clutching mobile phones, and a conversation about politics was raging on. The talk included the government, elections, development and a question about one absent person—“Where is our MP?”

This question was not merely about the absence of any one Member of Parliament. In a democracy, electing a representative is more than a political process. It is the beginning of a relationship between the citizen and power. Voters do not cast their vote and then simply sit at home. They expect their representative to carry their voice to Parliament, listen to their questions and demand answers from those in power.

But when the representative remains absent, citizens lose a bridge to power. In a democracy, absence itself is a political event. In the villages and bazaars of Madhesh, democracy is often felt not in grand constitutional words but in small experiences like this.

For the citizen sitting in Pipara bazaar, the constitution is not some distant book. When Parliament is made secondary, when the representative is cut off from the people and when the decision-making process becomes opaque, a constitutional crisis becomes the everyday experience of the citizen.

Democracy is sometimes understood less from the preamble of the Constitution and more from this ordinary experience of a citizen—that their voice is being heard somewhere and that the government is ready to dispel their fears. The truth is that the ruling MPs are avoiding the people. There is no dialogue between them and the government. Indeed, this crisis is not limited to Nepal.

In many democracies of the world, elected governments, after assuming power, appear uncomfortable with three things: limits, questions and the future. Limits remind them that even after winning an election, they are not all-powerful. Questions remind them that a popular mandate is not synonymous with objective truth. And the future reminds them that today’s power cannot control the generations to come. Authoritarian governments do not accept any kind of limit at all.

But in a democracy, elected government must be accountable to the constitution, the judiciary, the Parliament, the press and civil society. A majority mandate gives them unlimited power. Then gradually, they begin to believe that no one should question them. However, in democracy, an elected government can and should be questioned by the people.

What I have earlier called a dopamine government—a government that constantly builds its political self-confidence on immediate achievements, visible results and popular excitement—faces a major crisis precisely in this. It tends to treat the popular mandate as a certificate of freedom from accountability. The intoxication of electoral success gradually makes it believe that popularity is morality, majority is truth and electoral victory is proof of authority over all institutions.

Today, a traditional military coup is not always necessary to weaken democracy. Democratic institutions are sometimes weakened through the very institutions and power structures that are considered guardians of the state’s stability. The erosion of democracy no longer comes wearing a uniform; sometimes it arrives by striking a deal with elected power.

The press sees this erosion first. That is why elected governments fear it. The press has no army, no police, no power to collect taxes—only questions. And questions are a regime’s greatest discomfort. The fear exists because the journalist asks: Why was this decision taken? Who will benefit from it? Who will pay its price? Is what the government said true? But the government, it does not like questions. It has to be answerable to citizens, but it hesitates.

That is why the methods of weakening the independent press have also changed. Sometimes the elected government need only plant a small fear in the journalist’s mind, and they begin to think: Will it be alright to publish this news? Will there be any trouble after this question? Is this the time to confront the government? When a journalist begins to think about their own existence before writing, it is evident that the crisis of press freedom has already begun.

While the elected government doesn’t think beyond the next election, some phenomena allow no such short-sightedness. One such phenomenon is the climate crisis. The former wants immediate results, but the latter warns of slow destruction, forcing us to think about future generations. The government demands roads, buildings, inaugurations and visible achievements. But climate poses it with uncomfortable questions: Who will pay the price for this development? Given its indifference to such questions, the current government’s apathy to the climate crisis is increasingly becoming apparent. When it deems environmental warnings as ‘anti-development’, and natural resources as ‘undeveloped’, development is reduced to mean more construction, more consumption and more extraction.

Nature speaks, but it has no vote. This is why those most vulnerable in a democracy are often those who cannot vote—future generations, displaced communities, dying ecosystems and the poor who bear the heaviest burden of the climate crisis.
